title: oncall-handoff-temp-procedures-ada-lopez
content:
Shift summary (2026-02-28 -> 2026-03-01)

Quick context:
- Took over from Noah at 09:00 PST. Quiet morning except for a noisy alert storm (see Alerts below).
- Production latency slightly elevated for /v1/generate (p50 ~220ms, baseline ~160ms) starting ~10:30 -> correlates with a batch of longer sequences from a single client (customer: acme-corp).
- No full outages. No PagerDuty escalations beyond P2.

Open items / what I did:
- Investigated elevated latency:
  - Checked recent deploys: none in prod in last 6 hours (deploy pipeline OK).
  - Top clients by request size: acme-corp spikes; asked solutions-eng to verify workload change (sent DM to @maya).
  - Temporary mitigation: enforced per-route token limit for acme-corp via rate-limiter for 1 hour (policy id: rl-2026-02-acme).
- Alerts: alert flapping from redis-cache-read-errors on rdb-02 (transient). Restarted rdb-02 container -> errors stopped. Raised OPS-421 to track root cause.
- KV cache warm-up: observed cache misses after midnight vacuum job; warming in progress (background worker).

Active incidents / pages:
- OPS-421: redis-cache-read-errors (P2) — assigned to Noah. Summary: transient IOError on rdb-02 during scheduled maintenance window, restarted container. Follow-up: confirm stability and check kernel logs for OOM events.

Immediate runbook notes (temporary procedures to use while we iterate on permanent fixes):
1) If /v1/generate latency spikes for multiple routes:
   - Check recent deploys: https://ci.redwood.com/pipelines (if deploy within last 30m, rollback option documented in deploy-runbook).
   - Run: kubectl top pods -n redwood-prod | sort -r -k2 (look for CPU outliers).
   - Check model workers queue length: curl -s http://svc-model-router.internal/metrics | grep queue_size
   - Temporary throttle: update rate-limiter config (k8s secret rl-config) to reduce max_tokens_per_call for offending client. Note: use canary policy first.

2) If Redis read errors repeat on rdb-0x:
   - SSH to host (if Dedicated): ssh ops@rdb-host-XX; tail /var/log/syslog and /var/log/docker.log for OOM or disk I/O errors.
   - kubectl rollout restart statefulset/redis-cluster -n infra; monitor for replication lag: redis-cli -h rdb-01 info replication
   - If replication lag > 10s and errors persist, escalate to infra oncall (pagerduty: infra-duty).

3) If streaming responses drop connections intermittently:
   - Check ingress LB health: aws elb describe-instance-health --name prod-ingress-lb
   - Confirm websocket proxy (ws-proxy) pods: kubectl get pods -n ingress -l app=ws-proxy -o wide
   - Rotate proxy: kubectl rollout restart deploy/ws-proxy -n ingress (do one replica group at a time).

Commands & quick checks (copy/paste):
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-prod -o wide
- kubectl logs deploy/model-worker -n redwood-prod --since=1h | grep ERROR | tail -n 200
- curl -sS https://api.redwood.com/health | jq .
- curl -s http://svc-model-router.internal/metrics | grep queue_size

Notes to self / TODOs (follow up later):
- TODO: add a permanent gating policy for unusually long sequence requests (proposal drafted in OPS-421).
- TODO: add runbook section for model-quantization-fallback behavior (observed two fallback events last week).
- Ask Platform Eng: can we add a metric for per-client rolling median token length? (ticket: PLAT-989)

Unresolved questions / rough ideas (notes/drafts):
- Could we have a short-lived global per-client token throttle that activates only when p95 latency > 300ms for 5m? Implementation complexity might be high but would save emergency throttles.
- Consider a lightweight on-call UI that shows top 10 clients by average tokens in last 15m (for SRE quick triage).

Useful links / references:
- Incident playbook (canonical): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/Incident-playbook
- OPS-421 (redis): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-421
- Deploy pipeline: https://ci.redwood.com/pipelines
- Slack channel: #sre-oncall (ping @infra-oncall for infra escalations)

Handoff checklist for next oncall:
- Review open Jira issues assigned to "oncall" label (query: label = oncall AND assignee in (current))
- Check queued alerts in Opsgenie / PagerDuty (filter: last 24h)
- Verify no ongoing rate-limits are applied to customers (k8s secret rl-config) — if present, leave a note and remove only after approval from product/security.

End notes: leaving this as draft — will formalize parts that become recurrrent. If anything spikes after I sign off at 17:00 PST, I will leave a short update in this doc and ping the followup oncall.

Ada Lopez (eng-sre)
